t.1.197.1: O king, you must surely be told by your kinsmen what is truly for your good; but words do not take root among those who do not wish to listen.
t.1.197.2: For Bhīṣma Śāṃtanava, best of the Kurus, has spoken words that are for your good, O king, and yet you do not accept them.
t.1.197.3: Thus Droṇa has spoken in many ways what is beneficial and excellent, yet Karṇa, the son of Rādhā, does not regard it as beneficial for you.
t.1.197.5: For these two are advanced in age, in wisdom and in learning, and they are impartial toward you, O king of kings, and toward those sons of Pāṇḍu as well.
t.1.197.4: Even on reflection, O king, I do not see anyone who is a better friend to you than these two lions among men, or anyone who would surpass them in wisdom.
t.1.197.6: In dharma and in truthfulness, O king, O Bhārata, these two are not inferior to Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, nor to Gaya; of this there is no doubt.
t.1.197.7: Never before have these two said anything to your detriment, nor is any wrong done by them against you to be seen.
t.1.197.8: These two tigers among men, O king, whose prowess is true, how could they not counsel what is good for you, who are blameless toward them?
t.1.197.9: These two are wise, the best of men in this world, O lord of men; therefore they will say nothing crooked on your account. Such is my firm conviction, O joy of the Kurus.
t.1.197.10: Nor will these two knowers of dharma speak in a partisan way for the sake of gain, for they have deemed this the highest good for you, O Bhārata.
t.1.197.11: O king, just as Duryodhana and the others are your sons, so too are those Pāṇḍavas your sons, O king; of this there is no doubt.
t.1.197.12: If your counselors, out of ignorance, should advise anything harmful against them, then those counselors of yours surely do not discern what is good for you.
t.1.197.13: But if, O king, there is partiality in your heart regarding them, then those who lay bare what lies within would surely not bring about your good.
t.1.197.14: For this reason, O king, these two great-souled and greatly splendid men did not speak anything openly, for this is not your resolve.
t.1.197.16: For how, O king, could the glorious Pāṇḍava, the ambidextrous archer, the scorcher of foes, be conquered in battle even by Maghavan?
t.1.197.15: And what those two bulls among men have declared about them, that they cannot be overcome, is truly so, O tiger among men; may it be well with you.
t.1.197.17: Bhīmasena, the mighty-armed, great and possessing the strength of ten thousand elephants, how indeed could he be conquered in battle even by the immortals?
t.1.197.19: How could he be conquered in battle, that best of the Pāṇḍavas in whom steadfastness, compassion, forbearance, truth and valor are ever present?
t.1.197.18: Likewise the twins, skilled in war like the sons of Yama: how could anyone who wishes to live withstand them in battle?
t.1.197.20: Those whose partisan is Rāma, whose counselor is Janārdana, and on whose side stands Sātyaki, what is there in battle that they could not conquer?
t.1.197.21: They whose father-in-law is Drupada, and whose brothers-in-law are the Pārṣatas, the heroic brothers, sons of Drupada, headed by Dhṛṣṭadyumna.
t.1.197.22: Recognizing that they cannot be overcome in open confrontation, O Bhārata, and that by dharma they have the right to inheritance, behave rightly toward them.
t.1.197.23: This great disgrace that has smeared you, the work of Purocana, wash it away from yourself today, O king, by showing them your favor.
t.1.197.25: The Dāśārhas are mighty and many, O lord of the people; where Kṛṣṇa is, there they would be, and where Kṛṣṇa is, there is victory.
t.1.197.24: Drupada too is a great king, and in the past he was made our enemy; winning him over, O king, will strengthen our own side.
t.1.197.26: And when a task can be accomplished by conciliation alone, O king, what man, cursed by fate, would set about doing it by means of war?
t.1.197.27: Having heard that the Pārthas are alive, the people of the city and the countryside are intensely eager to see them; O king, do what is pleasing to them.
t.1.197.28: Duryodhana and Karṇa, and Śakuni Saubala too, are bound to unrighteousness, evil-minded and childish; do not follow their words.
t.1.197.29: This was told by me to you, O king, virtuous as you are, long ago: through the offense of Duryodhana these people will perish.
